# `Tree`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Tree — a minimal recursive, payload-carrying ADT.

`Tree` is the synthetic proof that a kernel can return a recursive,
payload-carrying, runtime-backed stdlib ADT that user code constructs and
`case`-matches (issue #2493).  The type is a veneer over the runtime enum
`ipe_runtime::tree::Tree`; its `Leaf`/`Node` constructors and pattern matches
lower directly to that enum.  Recursion rides the `List` lowering — a `Node`
holds a `List Tree` of children, so no self-referential boxing is needed at
the bridge boundary.

Example:

    import Ipe.Tree as Tree exposing (Tree(..))

    depth : Tree -> Int
    depth tree =
        case tree of
            Leaf _ ->
                1

            Node children ->
                1 + List.foldl (\c acc -> max acc (depth c)) 0 children

## `Tree`

A recursive, payload-carrying sum.  `Leaf` carries an `Int`; `Node` carries
its children as a `List Tree` (the recursive edge).

## `demoTree`

```ipe
demoTree : Int -> Tree
```

`demoTree n` — build a small fixed tree whose leaf payloads derive from `n`.
Total and allocation-bounded (the shape is fixed), so no input can make it
grow without bound.

## `parseTree`

```ipe
parseTree : String -> Result Error Tree
```

`parseTree s` — parse a tiny S-expression into a `Tree`, or fail with a
typed `Error`.  Grammar: a leaf is `L<int>` (e.g. `L7`, `L-3`); a node is
`(child child …)`.  This is a parse boundary: the untrusted `String` becomes
a typed `Tree` once, and every failure — malformed syntax OR nesting past the
depth ceiling — is a typed `Error`, never a panic or an unbounded allocation.
